sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Any 3D vector is a linear combination of basis vectors.
Meet the standard basis: i, j, and k vectors.
These define our 3D unit cube foundation.
animations: Fade in basis vectors i_hat (#FF5733), j_hat (#33FF57), and k_hat (#3357FF).
Label i_hat, j_hat, and k_hat clearly near their vectors.
Highlight i_hat, j_hat, and k_hat defining the 3D unit cube.

sections.title: Defining 3D Transformations (0:45-1:45)
lecture_lines: A linear transformation is defined by basis vector landing.
We represent this using a 3x3 matrix.
Columns show where i, j, and k move.
animations: Show a 3D grid with unit vectors i, j, k.
Animate a 3x3 matrix multiplication acting on the 3D space.
Trace the path of the basis vectors to their new positions.

sections.title: Core Concept: The Determinant (1:45-3:00)
lecture_lines: The determinant represents a scaling factor for volume.
Volume changes from V to V' under transformation.
Example: A matrix with determinant 2 doubles volume.
Stretching an object scales its total enclosed volume.
animations: Display a unit cube and its transformation to a parallelepiped.
Label V as the initial volume and V' as the final volume.
Show the determinant ratio: V' / V = det(M).
Scale the cube to show the volume doubling for det=2.
Highlight the volume expansion using color #FFFF33.

sections.title: Application: Rotation & Shear (3:00-4:15)
lecture_lines: Rotations preserve lengths and volumes in 3D.
Shear matrices create slide effects on grid layers.
Scaling transforms change overall dimensions of objects.
animations: Animate a 3D object rotating and label it 'Rotation'.
Animate a shear transformation and label it 'Shear'.
Animate a scaling transformation and label it 'Scale'.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: 3D transformations remap the entire 3D space grid.
The matrix is a recipe for basis movement.
Multiplication tracks complex character motion smoothly.
animations: Animate the grid transforming as the final summary.
Fade in the matrix formula: [a, b, c; d, e, f; g, h, i].
Display the determinant formula: det(M) = volume scaling factor.
